name: Sofpironium bromide (Sofdra)

lead: Sofpironium bromide is a topical gel applied to the underarms to reduce sweating in people with primary axillary hyperhidrosis. It was approved in Japan in 2020 as Ecclock and in the US in 2024 as Sofdra.

Its relevance to appearance is limited to visible sweat and sweat stains. Published trials are medical studies in people diagnosed with hyperhidrosis, and no community material on it was found in the sources reviewed.

paras: It is an anticholinergic: it blocks acetylcholine receptors (muscarinic M3) on eccrine sweat glands at the application site, which reduces the signal that triggers sweating. The US label describes it as a competitive inhibitor of acetylcholine receptors on tissues including sweat glands.

The US label lists dry mouth, blurred vision, application-site pain, redness and irritation, dilated pupils and urinary retention as the most common adverse reactions, and warns about urinary retention, lack of sweating in hot environments and transient blurred vision. It is prescription-only in the US and Japan.

lead: Sofpironium bromide is a topical anticholinergic medication for primary axillary hyperhidrosis, excessive underarm sweating without an underlying medical cause. It was developed by Bodor Laboratories, licensed to Brickell Biotech (development code BBI-4000), and approved in Japan in 2020 as Ecclock and in the US in 2024 as Sofdra. [1][2][3]

In looks-related contexts, hyperhidrosis matters mainly for visible sweating and sweat marks on clothing. Evidence for the product comes from medical trials in patients with diagnosed hyperhidrosis; it is a prescription product, not a cosmetic or over-the-counter item. [4][5][3]

Phase 2 and phase 3 randomized, vehicle-controlled trials have evaluated it, and a long-term open-label study in Japan followed patients for 52 weeks. A 2025 systematic review has also assessed its efficacy and safety. [4][5][6][7]
infobox: Bodor Laboratories; licensed to Brickell Biotech

paras: The US label indicates Sofdra for primary axillary hyperhidrosis in adults and in children aged 9 and older. [3] In Japan the 5% gel was approved for the same condition. [1]
Trials have also registered studies in palmar hyperhidrosis (phase 2) and in pediatric patients. [8][9]
Sweat glands are stimulated by acetylcholine acting on M3 muscarinic receptors. Sofpironium bromide is designed to inhibit those receptors at the site of application, which reduces sweating. [1][3]

According to the US label, the most common adverse reactions (2% or more) are dry mouth, blurred vision, application-site pain, erythema, dermatitis, pruritus and irritation, dilated pupils and urinary retention. [3]

The label's warnings cover use with caution in people with a history of urinary retention, watching for a general lack of sweating in hot environments, and avoiding driving or machinery if blurred vision occurs. [3] The label reports no adverse effects in animal reproduction studies at the doses tested and notes there are no data in pregnant women. [3]

A phase 2 randomized, double-blind trial tested three dosages against vehicle for 42 days in axillary hyperhidrosis. [5] A phase 3 vehicle-controlled trial in Japanese patients treated 5% gel for six weeks, with co-primary endpoints of a Hyperhidrosis Disease Severity Score of 1 or 2 and at least a 50% reduction in gravimetric sweat weight. [4]

A 52-week open-label study followed 185 patients who completed the confirmatory trial to assess long-term safety and efficacy. [6] A two-week observational study reported on use in routine practice in Japan. [10] Two US phase 3 trials (BBI-4000-CL-301 and CL-302) enrolled about 350 participants each. [11][12]
A 2025 systematic review and a 2022 review of topical anticholinergics summarize the evidence for the drug class and for sofpironium specifically. [13][7]

timeline.event: Phase 2 studies of BBI-4000 begin in axillary and palmar hyperhidrosis. [8][14]
First approval in Japan as Ecclock for primary axillary hyperhidrosis. [1]
US phase 3 trials CL-301 and CL-302 begin. [11][12]
